files in the writable workspace. Replace the stub in place in `Proof.lean`;
never declare another `def` with the same name anywhere else — a same-named
helper inside a namespace (for example `Operational.stringCodes` alongside
the `stringCodes` binding) counts as a second definition and fails the
mechanical gate before your proof is even checked. Give every helper a
distinct name.

A stub bound to a global dispatch symbol (`applyBin`, `applyCmp`,
`applyMethod`, `applyBuiltin`, or any symbol whose frozen rules span many
operator or method cases) must implement the COMPLETE frozen rule table for
that symbol — every operator, operand-sort combination, and coercion the
frozen semantics defines — not only the cases the target exercises. A
catch-all arm returning a degenerate constant (`noneV`, `false`, `0`) where
the frozen semantics has a concrete rule misrepresents the symbol and is a
failed proof: the independent audit executes the frozen semantics on
operators outside your theorem's path and rejects any divergence.

The completeness obligation is bounded by the immutable Base's value
universe. If the Base omits an injection (for example, `SortVal` has no
string injection), frozen rules over that sort cannot be represented and
are outside the fixed dispatcher's domain: omit them and continue. Do not
refuse the proof because unrepresentable rules exist — the independent
audit judges completeness relative to the generated trust, not against
sorts the Base cannot express.

That bound is not a license to shrink the domain further. Every value the
Base CAN represent must receive its frozen meaning — this applies to every
bound symbol, not only dispatchers. A sorting, comparison, or summary
function restricted to integers with an identity or constant fallback on
representable Booleans, strings, or sequences the frozen rules do handle
is a failed proof; the audit evaluates exactly such representable
non-integer witnesses.

Hooked operations (Float min/max, rounding, division, modulo, string
ordering) must implement the behavior of the frozen K hooks, read from the
mounted semantics — never assumed from IEEE conventions or Lean library
defaults. Edge cases routinely differ: K 7.1.293 `maxFloat` returns the
non-NaN operand, `%Int` is truncated (`Int.tmod`), not Euclidean. The
audit evaluates precisely these edge inputs against the frozen hooks.

When a frozen symbol is partial or divergent on part of its domain, choose
ONE fixed totalization and keep the symbol's frozen equations valid on
every state its guards cover — including artificial or unreachable states.
State-dependent convenient values (a different fallback per divergent
state, chosen to close the theorem) break the universal frozen rule and
fail the audit even when every reachable case is correct.

A trusted opaque symbol documented as a total ordering or sort (for
example an "ascending sort" over `ValSeq`) must actually order every
representable comparable sequence by the source program's comparison
semantics — Booleans sort with `false < true`, strings by code sequence,
integers numerically. Concrete frozen rules existing only for some
element sorts do not make identity acceptable on the others: the audit
executes representable Boolean and mixed sequences and rejects any
implementation that leaves them unsorted.

Run `lake build`. The final writable proof must contain no `sorry`, `admit`,
`unsafe`, new `axiom`, new `opaque`, or altered target statement. Do not change
the pinned toolchain or dependency configuration. Report the remaining trusted
declarations from the generated Klean base, but do not treat them as proof
goals you may assume through a new shortcut.

End your final response with exactly one completion marker on its own line:

`RESULT: LEAN_PROOF_COMPLETE — <brief summary>`

Replace the angle-bracketed text with a short nonempty summary. No other line
may begin with `RESULT:`.

import Klean95CheckDictCase.Lemmas

namespace Operational

/- The K `==K` used by list.count and tuple.index is structural equality.
   Derive it for the entire generated mutual carrier so those method rules
   cover every value Base can represent, not merely integers. -/
deriving instance BEq for SortIntSeq
deriving instance BEq for SortExc, SortExcCell, SortEnvCell,
  SortExitCodeCell, SortGeneratedCounterCell, SortHeapLocCell, SortOptInt,
  SortScopeLocCell, SortParamNames, SortCellVars, SortFreeVars, SortParams
deriving instance BEq for
  SortApplyK, SortBound, SortCmpOp, SortEntries, SortEntry, SortExpr, SortExprs,
  SortGeneratedTopCell, SortHeapCell, SortIndex, SortIterable, SortK, SortKCell,
  SortKItem, SortList, SortMap, SortModule, SortRetCell, SortRetState,
  SortScopesCell, SortStackCell, SortStmt, SortStmts, SortVal, SortValSeq, SortVals

def emptyCodeSequence : SortIntSeq :=
  SortIntSeq.«.IntSeq_MPY-CORE_IntSeq»

def isUpperCode (code : SortInt) : SortBool :=
  decide (65 ≤ code ∧ code ≤ 90)

def isLowerCode (code : SortInt) : SortBool :=
  decide (97 ≤ code ∧ code ≤ 122)

def hasUpperCode : SortIntSeq → SortBool
  | SortIntSeq.«.IntSeq_MPY-CORE_IntSeq» => false
  | SortIntSeq.«iCons(_,_)_MPY-CORE_IntSeq_Int_IntSeq» code rest =>
      isUpperCode code || hasUpperCode rest

def hasLowerCode : SortIntSeq → SortBool
  | SortIntSeq.«.IntSeq_MPY-CORE_IntSeq» => false
  | SortIntSeq.«iCons(_,_)_MPY-CORE_IntSeq_Int_IntSeq» code rest =>
      isLowerCode code || hasLowerCode rest

def valuesStructurallyEqual (left right : SortVal) : SortBool :=
  left == right

def countValueOccurrences : SortValSeq → SortVal → SortInt
  | SortValSeq.«.ValSeq_MPY-CORE_ValSeq», _ => 0
  | SortValSeq.«vCons(_,_)_MPY-CORE_ValSeq_Val_ValSeq» head tail, sought =>
      (if valuesStructurallyEqual head sought then 1 else 0) +
        countValueOccurrences tail sought

def indexOfValueFrom : SortValSeq → SortVal → SortInt → Option SortInt
  | SortValSeq.«.ValSeq_MPY-CORE_ValSeq», _, _ => none
  | SortValSeq.«vCons(_,_)_MPY-CORE_ValSeq_Val_ValSeq» head tail, sought, index =>
      if valuesStructurallyEqual head sought then some index
      else indexOfValueFrom tail sought (index + 1)

def fixedUndefinedMethodValue : SortVal :=
  SortVal.«noneV_MPY-CORE_Val»

/- Complete applyMethod table relative to Base's carrier.

   Base can represent list and tuple receivers and Int results, so list.count
   and tuple.index are included.  Base has no SortStr/inj_SortStr constructor;
   consequently all string-receiver rules and md5Obj.hexdigest's string result
   are unrepresentable and outside this fixed dispatcher's domain.  Every
   combination not covered by a representable guarded equation receives the
   same fixed totalization. -/
def dispatchRepresentableMethod : SortVal → SortString → SortVals → SortVal
  | SortVal.inj_SortIterable
      (SortIterable.«list(_)_MPY-CORE_Iterable_ValSeq» values), method,
      SortVals.«_,__MPY-CORE_Vals_Val_Vals» argument
        SortVals.«.List{"_,__MPY-CORE_Vals_Val_Vals"}_Vals» =>
      if method == "count" then
        SortVal.inj_SortInt (countValueOccurrences values argument)
      else fixedUndefinedMethodValue
  | SortVal.inj_SortIterable
      (SortIterable.«tuple(_)_MPY-CORE_Iterable_ValSeq» values), method,
      SortVals.«_,__MPY-CORE_Vals_Val_Vals» argument
        SortVals.«.List{"_,__MPY-CORE_Vals_Val_Vals"}_Vals» =>
      if method == "index" then
        match indexOfValueFrom values argument 0 with
        | some index => SortVal.inj_SortInt index
        | none => fixedUndefinedMethodValue
      else fixedUndefinedMethodValue
  | _, _, _ => fixedUndefinedMethodValue

end Operational

requires "reference-semantics/semantics.k"

module PROOF-THEORY
  imports MPY

  // Attribute-complete twin of the frozen isStrV discriminator.  The two
  // equations are exhaustive over Val and exactly duplicate its constructor
  // and owise cases; unlike isStrV, this declaration tells the backend it may
  // soundly split a symbolic result.
  syntax Bool ::= isStringKey(Val) [function, total]
  rule isStringKey(str(_:IntSeq)) => true
  rule isStringKey(_:Val) => false [owise]

  // Derived equation between the frozen partial declaration and the
  // attribute-complete twin.  Both sides have the same exhaustive equations.
  rule isStrV(V:Val) => isStringKey(V) [simplification]

  // Observed only when isStringKey(V) is true.  On that complete domain V is
  // str(CS), so the constructor equation uniquely determines the codes.
  syntax IntSeq ::= stringCodes(Val)
                    [function, total, symbol(stringCodes), no-evaluators]
  rule stringCodes(str(CS:IntSeq)) => CS [simplification]

  syntax Bool ::= lowerKeyCodes(IntSeq) [function, total]
                | upperKeyCodes(IntSeq) [function, total]

  rule lowerKeyCodes(CS:IntSeq)
    => hasLower(CS) andBool notBool hasUpper(CS)
  rule upperKeyCodes(CS:IntSeq)
    => hasUpper(CS) andBool notBool hasLower(CS)

  syntax Bool ::= lowerKey(Val) [function, total]
                | upperKey(Val) [function, total]

  rule lowerKey(V:Val) => lowerKeyCodes(stringCodes(V))
    requires isStringKey(V)
    [simplification]
  rule lowerKey(V:Val) => false
    requires notBool isStringKey(V)
    [simplification]

  rule upperKey(V:Val) => upperKeyCodes(stringCodes(V))
    requires isStringKey(V)
    [simplification]
  rule upperKey(V:Val) => false
    requires notBool isStringKey(V)
    [simplification]

  syntax Bool ::= foldLowerKeys(Bool, ValSeq) [function, total]
                | foldUpperKeys(Bool, ValSeq) [function, total]
                | allLowerKeys(ValSeq)        [function, total]
                | allUpperKeys(ValSeq)        [function, total]
                | hasAnyKey(ValSeq)           [function, total]

  rule foldLowerKeys(AL:Bool, .ValSeq) => AL
  rule foldLowerKeys(AL:Bool, vCons(V:Val, REST:ValSeq))
    => foldLowerKeys(AL andBool lowerKey(V), REST)

  rule foldUpperKeys(AU:Bool, .ValSeq) => AU
  rule foldUpperKeys(AU:Bool, vCons(V:Val, REST:ValSeq))
    => foldUpperKeys(AU andBool upperKey(V), REST)

  rule allLowerKeys(KS:ValSeq) => foldLowerKeys(true, KS)
  rule allUpperKeys(KS:ValSeq) => foldUpperKeys(true, KS)

  rule hasAnyKey(.ValSeq) => false
  rule hasAnyKey(vCons(_:Val, _:ValSeq)) => true

  syntax Bool ::= checkCaseSummary(Bool, Bool, Bool, ValSeq)
                  [function, total]
  rule checkCaseSummary(AL:Bool, AU:Bool, SEEN:Bool, KS:ValSeq)
    => (SEEN orBool hasAnyKey(KS))
       andBool
       (foldLowerKeys(AL, KS) orBool foldUpperKeys(AU, KS))
